- **Boundary:** Driver session socket (escher-driver)
  - **What to validate:** Request line from a local peer
  - **How (stack-specific):** One request line and one reply line per connection, `\n`-terminated, parsed against a closed grammar at wire version `v3` (`v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording): `hello v3`, `stop v3` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` — kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly (uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling); a known word with another version is answered `refused version`, anything else — a call the decoder does not read and a request line over 16,384 bytes included (was 64) — `refused malformed`, and runs nothing; a decoded call is run through `Session::run`, which validates it first (the Driver command schema row), and nothing else, and answered `ok v3 accepted <json>` or `ok v3 refused <json>`; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing, a connection that ends before a line terminator gets no reply, and a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written; one connection at a time, each read and write under a 2 s bound, a client's read of a call's answer under 30 s, pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout` — the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, and a read past it on a listener that never answers `SessionError::Timeout` (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:263-308); a lifecycle reply is bounded at 128 bytes and carries a pid, the session's label, a count and the idle expiry only; an answer is bounded at 1,048,576 bytes on its JSON line
 — over it the reply is `ok v3 oversize`, the call having run, and a call after which the host's recording ended is answered the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` in place of its answer, the call having run and read by the client as `SessionError::RecordingFailed` — and carries what the screen reads: ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text, the diff and a lint's findings, where until that chunk no reply carried any of them — the crossing ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label «Сокет несёт команды»; the English wording is the overseer's); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an answer also carries the screen as an image — an accepted `screenshot`'s line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}`, a PNG of the whole screen or of one element's visible part, a password input in it painted masked (the password row) — the pixels in band under the unchanged 1,048,576-byte bound (the largest whole-screen answer on the stand 22,404 bytes, 2.1 % of it), ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer); since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states those two carriers also hold three state readings for an element that states one — the snapshot's text up to five more bare words of a closed set (`selected` / `unselected`, `pressed` / `unpressed`, `invalid`), a diff node up to three more keys (`selected` and `pressed` written only where present, `invalid` always written, each a boolean; twelve node keys in the schema's order, thirteen since 2026-10-12-self-description added `differs` after `bounds` on a changed node only — a list of closed words, the node-key names read from `NODE_FIELDS` by index, an added node written without it
 — a closed value set inside the ratified carrier under the same rule, each `NODE_FIELDS` row now `{ name, help }`) — never an attribute's value as typed, with no carrier, verb, argument kind, refusal cause, log field, socket or port added, the wire staying `v2` and the request grammar and its bounds as they were: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing and not a further widening, on the founder's ruling (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer: inside the ratified crossing), which also sets the rule from that day on — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening and does not come to him, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still does (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:39-118; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:156-162; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:115-134 — the states as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md, `differs` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/report.md); no `NodeId` crosses; unix only, `Unsupported` elsewhere (packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:15-35; packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:179-211; packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:137-214) — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md, the call, its answers and the bounds at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md (51 malformed rows in the wire's unit tests; five raw lines outside the grammar and one wrong-version line through a live socket, each refused with nothing run; the answer bound held at its edge and one byte over)

- **Boundary:** Recorded check (escher-driver `Check::from_bytes`)
  - **What to validate:** A kept check's bytes, untrusted
  - **How (stack-specific):** Since 2026-10-19-session-recording a strict reader: at most 1,048,576 bytes, a JSON array of at most 400 records — the opening `{"tool":"start","arguments":{"app":…}}`, then records with the closed keys `tool` · `arguments` · `masked` · `accepted` · `digest` · `answer` only, `tool` one of the eight instance verbs, argument names from that verb's schema, `masked` true on a `type` alone, `digest` 16 lowercase hex and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, `answer` required and a JSON object (missing, a string, a number, an array or `null` refused; key order not enforced, read as a map); anything else refused `Cause::Malformed` with no fault, holding nothing of the file, with no panic path (40 refusal rows, 8 read rows and edge rows at both bounds); read by `serde_json`, which writes nothing, each `Call` built through `command::call_of`, the builder the MCP server shares, so a replayed step still passes `validate` inside `Session::run` — since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `Check::replay` runs each kept step's call through `Session::run` alone, nothing on a session of another app, and stops at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, its `Replay` and `Change` holding bools, counts and closed schema words only; the reader also reads the two committed checks under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` (`stand_replay`) (packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs:321-351; packages/escher-driver/src/replay.rs:40-70); the cold-agent pipe also reads its live child's kept checks — its `recording` step parses each numbered check with python `json`, a second reader beside `Check::from_bytes` that holds bools and counts only (`recorded_sessions`, `recording_kept`, the reason `recording-not-kept`), a directory it cannot read read as no check kept, no check's content printed or copied (scripts/cold-agent.sh:257-271)

- **Boundary:** CLI arguments (escher-session)
  - **What to validate:** A driver command: a verb, its arguments and the session's directory
  - **How (stack-specific):** Since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the argv is read by `escher_driver::command_line`, to which `main` hands it with the stand's six slugs (`counter`, `flight-booker`, `timer`, `crud`, `cells`, `load`, a closed six-entry `TASKS` table over the private `Served` enum) and the stand's boot; a closed reader with its rules in a fixed order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape or, since 2026-10-19-session-recording, with one `--record <dir>` after it, else usage; since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the first word `mcp` alone or with one `--record <dir>` selects the MCP role, and `mcp` with any other word after it — `mcp x`, `mcp --session d` — is usage; `--record <dir>` is taken at most once, on `start <app> --session <dir> --record <dir>`, the host role and the `mcp` role, and anywhere else, twice or with no value is usage, status 2, once the call passed `validate` (a refused call stays a refusal; a stray `--record` was an unnamed argument, status 1, before); `start` checks the recording directory before it spawns, a refusal status 3 with nothing spawned, and `mcp --record` before it serves, a refusal status 3 with its fixed message on stderr and stdout empty; the path is never written back (packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:40-42; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:160-165), the role handing stdin and stdout to `serve_mcp` with the binary's apps and `IDLE_EXPIRY` (the MCP server row below) and `command_line`'s `boot` an `FnMut` where it was `FnOnce` (packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:92); since 2026-10-12-self-description `help` with no argument and at most one `--session <dir>`, the directory not read, answers `describe()`'s one line of JSON on stdout, status 0, reaching no session, `help` with an argument (`help x`) is refused `malformed`, status 1, and `help --session` with no directory or given twice is usage, status 2
 — every text of the answer a fixed string of the schema's tables, and `help --verb click` writing back nothing it named (packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:178-183); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `screenshot` with an optional `--id` answers one line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` on stdout, status 0 — the image by the ratified in-band crossing (the founder, 2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», relayed verbatim by the overseer) — and `--id` on an id the screen does not read exits 1 writing nothing the caller typed (examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:374-417); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb` (the former two-argument form `<task> <state-dir>` reads so); the call the remaining words spell — an instance-level verb's arguments as flags spelt as the schema spells them, `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each followed by one value, whatever that word is, `--shift` bare, and `start`'s app as one plain word — is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for (the Driver command schema row); then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage; an argument that is not text is a usage error, and no path on argv panics; the state directory then passes `serve`'s checks above; four endings — accepted, the answer as one line of JSON on stdout, status 0; refused, the refusal on stdout, status 1; usage, one fixed line on stderr built from the verb table and the app names (`help` listed after `stop` since 2026-10-12-self-description, `screenshot` after `scroll` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot), stdout empty, status 2, nothing booted and no state created; session error, the error object on stdout — carrying the error's fixed `remedy` beside `kind` and `message` since 2026-10-12-self-description
 — and its fixed message on stderr, status 3 (the host role's was 1); the four statuses read from `EXIT_STATUSES` since that chunk — and the host role's quiet end, nothing written, status 0, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `mcp` role's end, nothing on stdout, status 0 on `Ok` and status 3 with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err`, the usage line naming the role (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`, beside `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`); no command's ending writes back anything the caller typed — no path, label, id or value — and an answer on stdout holds ids, names, values and, since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states, the three state readings (closed words in the snapshot's text, booleans in a diff node) and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's base64 PNG and a lint's findings by the ratified crossing (the Driver session socket row); a write to a closed pipe is dropped, not a panic — pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by `cli_commands`' `a_closed_stdout_drops_the_answer_and_keeps_the_ending`: with its stdout's read end closed before the run, `help` exits 0 and `snapshot --session {dir}` with no session exits 3 with exactly `SessionError::NoSession`'s fixed message on stderr, neither printing a panic, and no state directory is created (examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:649-711); `start` spawns the running binary again (`std::env::current_exe()`) as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, passing on a given `--record <dir>`, with its three streams closed, waits up to 30 s for the host to answer and neither kills nor reaps it; the command line installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable — a new external input surface, ratified by the founder with the crossing (2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option labels «Бинарник приложения, путь» · «Именованные флаги» · «Четыре класса»;
 the English wording is the overseer's) (examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:12-28; examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:34-56; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:137-203; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:215-275; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:304-338; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:456-476) — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md (61 rows of the reader's rules in its unit test; `host_binary` holds the usage line free of anything typed)

- **Boundary:** MCP server (escher-driver `serve_mcp`, the `escher-session mcp` role)
  - **What to validate:** JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and tool arguments from the MCP client that spawned the process, over that process's stdin
  - **How (stack-specific):** Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on the invoking user's stdin and stdout — no listener, port, socket, authentication or env read; a request line of at most 65,536 bytes (`MAX_MCP_REQUEST_BYTES`), a longer one read to its terminator, dropped and answered `-32700`; an empty line skipped; non-UTF-8 or non-JSON → `-32700`; not an object with `jsonrpc: "2.0"` and a string `method` → `-32600`; an `id` echoed only as an i64 integer or a string of at most 128 bytes, else `-32600` with `id: null` — the echo the one client-sent value written back; a protocol error a fixed code and a fixed message (`parse error` · `invalid request` · `method not found` · `invalid params` · `unknown tool`) with no `data`; `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` answered, every other method — `server/discover` included — `-32601`; since 2026-10-12-self-description `initialize`'s revision matched against a closed table of four (`2025-11-25` · `2025-06-18` · `2025-03-26` · `2024-11-05`), any other — `2026-07-28` and `2099-01-01` included — answered `2025-11-25` (the operator's answer at that chunk's plan forks; taking up `2026-07-28` left to a later version, the founder, 2026-10-12, «Не сейчас, в остатки», relayed verbatim by the overseer); `tools/list` the twelve verbs, `help` last (`screenshot` and `lint` among them, a `lint` tool call's result its JSON line `{"findings":[…]}`), each `description` the verb's help, then `. Returns: ` and each result field as `{name} ({kind}): {help}` — fixed table text, the listing 2,984 → 8,844 bytes; a `help` tool call answered by the server, held session or not, its text block `describe()`'s line, ending accepted, its `tool_call` span `tool` = `help` with no `command` child, counted in a held session's `served` (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp/listing.rs:50-59)
 — the program's own fixed `'static` text inside the ratified carrier, ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «Внутри, с правилом», relayed verbatim by the overseer); and a request with no `id` a notification: no reply, nothing runs; a `tools/call`'s `params` an object with a string `name` and an optional object `arguments`, else `-32602 invalid params`, a name outside `VERBS` `-32602 unknown tool`, each argument value a string → text, an i64 → number, a bool → flag, any other refused `malformed` before anything runs, then `validate` or `validate_session` (the Driver command schema row); `start` on an app outside the binary's six apps (`counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load`, its `app` enum listing them as the program's own fixed table text) refused `malformed`; arguments arrive in key order, so a repeated key collapses to its last value and `Repeated` cannot arise over MCP; a result's text over 1,048,576 bytes (`wire::MAX_ANSWER_BYTES`) replaced by `AnswerTooLarge`'s result — since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a result that holds an image bounded by its whole written form instead, a text-only result by its text as before (`ToolResult::bounded`); the idle expiry checked when a request arrives, no timer or thread; replies written by the crate's hand-written JSON writer only, `serde_json` reading and writing nothing — no print, `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside the tests (a probe over the module, count 0); results carry ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask) and the snapshot text and a lint's findings by the crossing and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, the screen as an image

text:
- **Boundary:** Markup attributes
  - **What to validate:** `aria-label` · `<label for>` (accessible names)
  - **How (stack-specific):** Read from parsed content — the browser app's remote HTML included — into the accessibility tree by an in-process reader; the parser already admits both, so no new input class enters: an `aria-label` non-empty after trimming becomes the node's `label` (accname-1.2 §2C) and a whitespace-only one names nothing; after the visit each built `<label>` resolves through `label_bound_input_element` (its `for`-target labelable element by id, else its first nested labelable element — HTML's labelable elements, `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden` (ASCII case-insensitive), `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` and `textarea`, by the private `is_labelable`, a closed element-name match) and is pushed onto that element's `labelled_by` only when both have built nodes, so a hidden label or element never associates and a hidden input is never named by one, and a click on a select's label re-dispatches to the select; since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync the builder also reads `aria-labelledby` as upstream wrote it: after the `<label>` → input loop it clears the node's `labelled_by`, pushes the referenced nodes that have built nodes (`referenced_dom_ids_to_node_ids`; an id naming no element ignored) and sets their text, gathered cycle-guarded through `write_text_alternative` · `write_flat_text_content` · `FlatText`, as the computed `label`, so it outranks a `<label>` and an `aria-label` (accname 2B), a hidden target's text read without the target referenced and the `aria-label` the fallback when the targets hold no text; upstream's own unfiltered `aria-label` read was dropped in the merge, so there is still one trimmed, non-empty `aria-label` read; the computed label reaches `label` and so the snapshot's `name`, and its page text stays inside the ratified name crossing below — the adapter, the driver's answers, MCP results
 — on the founder's «Утвердить оба (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-17, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer), pinned by `accessibility_label`'s 13 tests (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:62-103; packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:119-126; packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:276-327; tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_label.rs:30-297; tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_label.rs:299-440); no lookup panics; escher's own code logs no name, and a host that installs escher's sink writes none to stderr at any `RUST_LOG` level: the record that carried a name at `trace`, from the third-party target `dioxus_core::diff::node`, is outside the sink's allowlist and is dropped whole since 2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist — the instrument's name needles found on stderr at `trace`, before → after the drop: the `escher-session` binary on `crud` 6 of 6 → 0, the windowed `seven_guis_native` on Home 5 of 5 → 0, and 0 on both at the default level, `info` and `debug`; typed text in a host's log is measured since 2026-10-10-driver-cli: a hosted `type` reaches the `escher-session` host's instance through the socket's `call`, and a typed sentinel occurs 0 times in that host's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace`, with 0 id needles and 0 name needles, under both builds (`host_log` as `-p seven_guis` and as `--workspace`; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md); driven in process with the sink installed over a capture at `RUST_LOG=info` (`stand_act_spans`'s re-run child), the typed text occurs 0 times in the capture and 0 of 8 name needles are found, in both layout modes (the readings as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/evidence/by-level.md, the in-process capture at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md); the names reach the platform accessibility adapter like any text run
 — on change as well as on the adapter's initial request since 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07, as the `id` row records); under dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature `DioxusDocument::snapshot` resolves the same names in-process into `SnapshotNode.name` — a node's non-empty `label`, else its `labelled_by` targets' names, cycle-guarded — with no new input class and no crossing: the snapshot's one text form, `Snapshot::to_text`, writes that name as each line's quoted string in `str`'s `Debug` form (a name holding a line break or a `"` stays inside its one field) and neither the snapshot nor its text reaches a log or event, and a file only as a kept check's kept answers — since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay each answer kept whole, names in the snapshot text and diffs included, owner-only and never logged, and the two committed Counter checks in git (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-19, as the `id` row records); `Snapshot::diff` reads the same resolved names from two snapshots into `DiffNode.name` — a changed name is one of the five readings that mark a node changed — with no new input class; since 2026-10-07-act-by-id the caller a name is returned to can be the caller of the driver's `Session::run` — its `snapshot` command returns the text and its acting commands the diff — and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli that is a crossing: accessible names leave the process in a hosted call's answer, in the snapshot's text and in a diff's JSON nodes, over the session socket and on the `escher-session` client's stdout (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label «Сокет несёт команды», the English wording is the overseer's, as the `id` row records;
 until then both were returned to their caller only) and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, in MCP tool results on the `mcp` role's stdout (the same crossing, its MCP carrier ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»), and still reach no log — the `mcp` role's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace` holds 0 typed-sentinel occurrences, 0 id needles and 0 name needles under both builds (`mcp_log`, examples/seven_guis/tests/mcp_log.rs:51-266) (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:36-61; packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:151-163; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:677-715; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3126-3140; tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_names.rs:1-11; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:199-217; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs:53; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs:108)

  - **What to validate:** `aria-describedby` · `aria-description` (descriptions)
  - **How (stack-specific):** Read from parsed content — remote pages included — into the accessibility tree by the in-process builder since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync, as upstream wrote them; the parser already admits both: `aria-describedby`'s referenced built nodes are pushed as AccessKit `described_by`, resolved as `aria-labelledby`'s are (an id naming no element ignored, a target not in the accessibility tree excluded), and `aria-description`'s own text is written into AccessKit's description field — free page text, unbounded, not a closed set; the added lines hold no log site, print or panic path; the one exit is the platform accessibility adapter — the snapshot reads no description, so no driver or MCP carrier, verb, field, log field or span carries it; a fourth content class on the adapter crossing (the `id` row), a boundary widening by upstream merge ratified as upstream's behaviour by the founder (2026-10-17, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer, «Утвердить оба (Рекомендую)»; both sources confirmed on the wrap's card by his «Подтвердить все 10 (Рекомендую)», 2026-10-18, relayed by the overseer); escher routes no agent- or user-supplied input through it; unmeasured at an assistive technology like the states, that windowed witness owned by its `.andromeda/residuals.md` line; pinned by `accessibility_description`'s 3 tests (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:89-102; packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:214-241; tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_description.rs:8-93)
